text:
sara_support: FYI customer reported a spike in tail latency + ~5% 5xxs for EU traffic starting ~09:00 UTC. They say requests are landing in us-west. :rotating_light:

michael_oncall: any traces or X-Region header evidence?

sara_support: attaching the snippet from their trace (they forwarded our proxy access log):
```
10.1.4.22 - - [17/Mar/2026:08:58:03 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 200 1245 "-" "curl/7.85.0" "x-region: eu-west1" "via: envoy" cluster=service-redwood-eu upstream_cluster=service-redwood-us-west1 response_flags=-
```

nicole_networks: upstream_cluster=service-redwood-us-west1 even though header says eu-west1. looks like L7 routing picked wrong cluster. Could be header rewrite or route matcher bug.

jun_park: reproduce steps request sample?

sara_support: customer run curl:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \n  -H 'X-Region: eu-west1' \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
They then toggled eu-west pool to drain and expected fallback to eu-central but saw us-west instead.

michael_oncall: can you paste envoy access logs from our gateway for same timeframe (internal)? Also which routing policy is active: region-by-header or geo-ip?

nicole_networks: looking at the gateway config in prod: we have a L7 virtual_host with a header matcher: `X-Region` -> route to cluster named `service-redwood-{region}`. There's also a fallback route that uses `cluster_header_rewrite` to point to `service-redwood-default` when no match. There is a known older patch that rewrote Host header on fallback.

jun_park: found an access log from our gateway node:
```
[2026-03-17T08:58:03Z] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 200 - upstream_cluster:"service-redwood-us-west1" requested_region:"eu-west1" route_match:"X-Region=eu-west1" host_rewrite:"us-west1.internal"
```

michael_oncall: aha — host_rewrite looks wrong. If host_rewrite is applied to the fallback path, Envoy can select cluster by SNI/host header for certain cluster selection plugins. That would ignore the X-Region matcher on subsequent hops.

sara_support: customer also reported some 403s when routed to us-west since their token is region-scoped. they saw auth failures only when cross-region happened.

nicole_networks: hypothesis: 1) route matched on X-Region -> intended cluster eu-west1 2) on fallback we trigger host_rewrite to default cluster but the header rewrite persists to origin or to the next hop causing a mismatch and cluster selection on the upstream LB picks us-west. 3) client sees higher latency and some region-scoped auth errors.

jun_park: how to reproduce in our staging quickly? Can simulate by setting pool eu-west1 unhealthy and sending X-Region header.

michael_oncall: repro steps (staging):
1) set `service-redwood-eu-west1` out_of_service on gateway pool (or iptables drop)
2) curl with `-H 'X-Region: eu-west1'` repeatedly
3) watch envoy access log for `upstream_cluster` and `host_rewrite`

sara_support: we ran that and consistently hit us-west in staging too when fallback engaged.

nicole_networks: minimal config snippet that looks suspicious: 
```
route:
  match: { headers: [ { name: "X-Region", exact_match: "eu-west1" } ] }
  route:
    cluster_header: "x-cluster"
    host_rewrite: "eu-west1.internal"
    upgrade_configs: []
```
When cluster_header isn't present we fall back to default cluster but host_rewrite is still set. That was part of a previous canary change.

michael_oncall: root cause likely our fallback flow leaves host_rewrite set which interacts poorly with our internal origin LB (it uses host header mapping to map to region-specific upstreams). So effect: wrong upstream chosen.

jun_park: proposed fixes:
- quick patch: remove host_rewrite on the fallback route OR guard it behind a `when_cluster_set` condition.
- longer term: ensure cluster selection exclusively uses explicit cluster_header or header matcher, not host header on upstream LB.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for config change r-2026-03-17-1254 on 3 gateway nodes. rollouts: 1/3

nicole_networks: rolling the canary now. monitoring metrics: tail latency and cross-region 403s.

sara_support: customer confirmed reduced cross-region hits after we rolled canary to their edge (they're on eu region). They saw latency drop from ~320ms median to ~85ms. 403s went to 0.

michael_oncall: follow-ups: add an integration test that simulates fallback and asserts host header unchanged; add a short runbook entry for support to check `upstream_cluster` vs `requested_region` in logs and to escalate to eng-networking with those logs.

jun_park: filing a GH issue with repro steps + config diff. I'll add links to the canary and the exact access log snippets we used.

sara_support: thanks all, I'll update the customer's ticket with the root cause and mitigation notes. :white_check_mark:
